limitations: Finite-input equivalence to existing student arithmetic, not native quality.
Complete student graph timings exclude D3D12 integration and do not accelerate native NVIDIA execution.
Exact full-image results cover only the checked checkpoints, inputs and environment.
Intervals average ten consecutive graph replays; p95 is an interval-average percentile, not per-frame tail latency.
Measured execution of experimental students plus grade, excluding D3D12 integration. No native-runtime acceleration.
One static input and one device; other desktop GPU work is not controlled.
Native quality is not achieved; no checkpoint is accepted or installed.
Negative gradients at one checkpoint do not prove harmful interference, dominating gradients or high curvature.
Scene and photo groups use the same renderer objective. This is a two-domain PCGrad experiment, not replication of the paper's multi-task results.
The two new runs share architecture, data, seed, original learning-rate schedule, 4500 updates and 9000 sampled examples. Their budget is larger than the earlier 4500-example RGB baseline.
Only the gradient projection differs between the paired controls; paired sampling itself changes the scene/photo balance to 50/50.
All 46 training and 16 validation frames are static first-reset sample captures. No representative gameplay or temporal quality acceptance is claimed.
Validation remains outside fitting but informs research choices; it is not independent final acceptance.
Residual fusion preserves the separate FP16 multiplication and addition roundings in the tested cases. It remains disabled by default and has no backward implementation.
The initial scalar implementation was slower. The final dense path uses aligned, contiguous channel-last pairs and keeps the scalar path for other layouts.
Alternating timings average ten replays per interval and reduce order sensitivity. Their percentiles are not individual-frame tail latencies.
Full 1080p student-plus-grade graphs exclude D3D12 integration. Student execution gains do not accelerate the native NVIDIA runtime.
No sample or game launches, no game/driver/native model or normal runtime changes.
